newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Elders expects to improve on 95/96.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Elders expects to improve on 95/96.

text.p: Pastoral house Elders Australia Ltd said on Thursday that it was tracking ahead for the first six months of 1996/97 compared with the previous year, and looking at a better result for the full year.
"Our profit for Elders in the first six months is better than at this time last year," chairman Alan Newman told Reuters after the company's annual general meeting.

"Last year's first half earnings were dramatically improved by the acquisition of (Australian Agricultural Co). That has not been the case in this year, yet the agency business is well ahead of where it was this time last year," Newman said.
Newman said he expected the first half improvement to continue through the full year. "We will do better I think unless there is a major deterioration in the second half," he said.

Newman told shareholders that minority stakeholders Marathon Asset Management and Sir James Goldsmith's General Oriental Investment Ltd would be offered a seat on the company's board to protect thier interests.
He later told Reuters the two investors had indicated they would not accept Futuris's takeover offer due to expire on December 20, and confirmed that Futuris would not raise its bid.
Futuris is offering 10 of its shares for every nine Elders shares plus 23 cents per Elders share.
Newman also said Elders would in the next few days announce further divestment of assets which were surplus to its requirments.
